judge.name: Contributor 25
judge.method: One independent exhaustive reading of the current content and whole current bar. No handler or screen implementation, test, score, or coverage report was read; no pack was executed. Previous verdicts were context only. This is the newly authorized judgment, not a carry-forward or second judging of applied changes.

barItemsRead: a refusal without a cause the story shows, or the same cause drawn twice; a run of refusals;
a failing repeat of a request that succeeded earlier in the same sitting;
a state switched away and back in one sitting, or returned with no reason the story shows;
a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept (a container made "to analyse" data that never runs the analysis, a comparison started and never finished);
a feature tour: one call per option of an endpoint in a row;
a read-back with no need: a list or get of what the story already holds, unless someone who does not hold it reads it;
the wrong actor or credential for an act, a date that contradicts the `wait` steps, a name or id used before it is made or after it is gone;
the wrong era: building on an API the vendor had deprecated by the World's date, or calling one past its documented shutdown;
vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts;

content that does not bear out the step's name: the code a push carries does not do what the story says it does, an upload carries no bytes of the file it names, a message the vendor never sends in that mode is said to arrive, an attachment lacks what its format requires;

a call through a door the vendor does not document (a path the client builds instead of the one the vendor returned, a read the vendor would refuse for want of a grant the story never gives), even where the twin answers it.

retainedAccountAssessment.reason: The original Orbit Apps organization is created at step 26, renamed Orbit Apps Inc. at step 37, and is never deleted. Kenji alone is removed at step 89; Priya remains its owner. Step 91 creates a distinct pilot under the same product with Priya as owner and captures pilot_org. Step 94 deletes that captured pilot id only, after step 93 obtains a current organizations token. The still-live original organization supplies a known subject for refresh and a parent for member/invitation reads. This follows the product source and the new RECIPE requirement without inventing an enumeration endpoint or emptying the product account.

stepNumbering: Every numeric steps, applySteps, contextSteps and reviewedStepIndices entry is a ZERO-BASED index in the exact 95-step customer-life.json identified by sha256. Only applySteps names required changes.

rulings.defect: Kenji opens the device verification page without his session cookie, but the step expects the signed-in page containing the user code. The following approval uses his cookie; the page visit must use that same browser session.
evidence: Architecture, Who is on a screen: the vendor session cookie names the person to every page after sign-in; a page asked for by nobody signed in sends its visitor to sign-in, and the journey carries the cookie as a browser would.

Pinned vendor ui-source.txt, devicePage: it first calls client.getSession(); without session.data it navigates to /login?return_to=... and returns before constructing or rendering the user-code input.

Judged steps[42] captures kenji_session on 9 January; auth-source.txt grants a 30-day session, so it is still valid at steps[52] on 10 January. Judged steps[53] already sends that exact session cookie.
rulings.fix: In the judged steps[52], add headers: { "cookie": "volter-id.session_token={kenji_session}" }. Keep method GET, path {device_link}, status 200 and its existing {ucode} expectation. This is Kenji using the laptop browser already signed in at steps[42] to approve the browserless build machine. Keep steps[53] and every wait unchanged. The only required changed life index for this ruling is 52.

doubts.reason: The World login submissions contain an email but no provider or email-code proof. The outline and manifest deliberately place first-sign-in proofs behind World doors and let the login screen stand in for the provider flow. That abstraction is therefore a stated precondition of this life, but these requests do not independently demonstrate possession of the identity. The vendor sources require provider, OTP or passkey proof; this judgment must not be read as evidence that the real vendor supports email-only sign-in.

The steps that say verification expose only JWKS retrieval, and Twin has no explicit JWKS retrieval before its first userinfo request. They do not independently prove signature, audience, expiry or nonce verification. At step 46 the prior access-token exchange has not requested the Teams resource; provider-source.txt distinguishes such opaque access tokens from resource JWTs, and step 48 obtains the Teams resource token later. Reading public keys is itself valid, so the evidence is insufficient for a further response-level ruling.

RH2 asks to sign in as someone else, but the story has not named a prior RH2 user and the identity-service cookie already identifies Priya. A previous application account on a shared console could explain the request. prompt=login is supported, so this is missing context rather than a vendor contradiction.

The phone reuses the session captured during the console sign-in. The story calls this an existing Volter session without showing how that particular bearer cookie reaches the phone. The supplied sources do not bind the cookie to a device, so provenance is unclear but a vendor refusal is not established.

Adding Kenji as member and immediately promoting him has little stated motivation. Granting administration during an engineer onboarding is plausible, and this is a one-way change rather than a state toggle.

The person lookup and invitation summaries partly repeat information already present in the preceding answers. The outline supplies directory resolution and an outstanding-invitations view as product needs; it could distinguish the reader or decision more explicitly. That stated application workflow is sufficient to avoid a categorical unnecessary-read ruling.

The members assertion relies on positional ordering. The vendor orders by createdAt, while the two memberships are created in the same frozen-World sitting with no wait. The supplied source does not state a tie-breaker; a membership-set assertion would be stronger evidence, but no contradictory vendor result is established here.

barAssessment: Refusals: the two authorization_pending answers concern separately created, still-unapproved device requests; the Apple refusal is caused by the explicitly unconfigured provider. No unexplained failure or hostile input is presented as normal success.
Repeats: no successful request is repeated as a failure in its sitting. Device polls follow the approval and five-second wait.
Toggles: promotion, rename, cancellation, departure and pilot retirement are one-way changes with stated causes; the original organization stays live.

Causes and promises: the invitations, product sign-ins, device approvals, employee departure and canceled pilot follow the stated customer arc. Cryptographic-verification evidence is limited as stated in doubts.
Feature tours: multiple registrations correspond to distinct demanded products; public/confidential and page/visitor/device flows have separate users, programs or occasions.
Read-backs: Kenji reads a team created by Priya; his selectors follow actual membership changes; directory and pending-invitation views have the stated product uses, subject to the listed doubts.

Actors, credentials, dates and identities: operator calls use both the browser session and admin bearer token; organizations calls use Twin client credentials rather than personal access; resources and redirects are registered first; opaque ids and codes are captured. The missing page cookie is ruled. Every dated wait and weekday agrees with the World clock.
Era: no supplied vendor evidence establishes a retirement or incompatible release date for any used operation. The source version alone does not prove a historical release date.

Vendor behavior: grants, scopes, resource links, PKCE, response fields, one-hour access lifetimes, 30-day refresh/session windows, seven-day invitations, five-second polls and ten-minute device-code windows were compared with the spec and pinned sources. All six verifier/challenge pairs match.

Content and names: request bodies, encoded fields, captures and expectations were read, including the configured-absent Apple input and the distinct captured pilot id. The verification claims and proof abstraction have the limitations stated in doubts.

Doors and captures: setup is explicitly behind World-only doors, product mutations use the published API, and returned hosted continuation and verification URLs are captured. The pilot deletion uses the captured pilot id rather than the original organization or a guessed id.
assessment: All 95 steps were read against every current bar item and the supplemental rules. The retained-account revision is plausible and satisfies the new known-refresh requirement. The one established life defect is the missing session cookie at zero-based step 52; the required repair is exact and confined to that step. The remaining concerns are explicitly doubts, not additional rulings. This assessment is from documents and static data only; no walk, suite, runtime result or implementation was used.
